title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to a typescript of P. Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques : formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', published in Modular Functions of One Variable IV (LNM 476, 1975). The section numbering (6.8, 7, Prop. 7.1, formula 2.5, curve 1.3) and the content match that text. It is a copy kept in Grothendieck's papers, not a text written by Grothendieck.

(1) End of §6, characteristic 2. Changes of Weierstrass coordinates x = u^2x' + r, y = u^3y' + su^2x' + t, restricted to those preserving the curve, form a group scheme with the stated composition law. For the supersingular j=0 curve in normal form (6.8), y^2 + y = x^3 (a3 = 1), the automorphism equations reduce to u ∈ μ3, s ∈ F4 and t^2 + t = s^3. Here s^3 equals 0 or 1 according as s = 0 or s ≠ 0, and r is determined by s (r = s^2). This gives 3·4·2 = 24 automorphisms, the group SL2(F3) ≅ Q8 ⋊ Z/3, the known maximal automorphism group in characteristic 2.

(2) §7, integral modular forms. A modular form of weight n over Z is a rule assigning to every generalized elliptic curve (genus one curve) E/S a section of ω^{⊗n}, compatibly with base change. Equivalently, one may restrict to curves without additive fibres.

Proposition 7.1: the ring of such forms is Z[c4, c6, Δ]/(c4^3 − c6^2 − 1728Δ).

Proof sketch begun on the page. Evaluating on the universal Weierstrass curve (1.3) over Z[a1, …, a6] shows that a form is an isobaric polynomial of weight n in the a_i, invariant under the coordinate-change group. After inverting 6, (2.5) shows the invariants are Z[1/6][c4, c6], so no further relations hold. It remains to show: a polynomial in c4, c6, Δ that vanishes identically in characteristic 2 (resp. 3) is divisible by 2 (resp. 3) in Z[c4, c6, Δ]/(relation). The continuation on the next page uses that a1 and ±b2 are the Hasse invariants in characteristics 2 and 3.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The composition law is written in the typescript's own conventions; within the j=0 normal form, r is tied to s (r = s^2), which the page leaves implicit.
The marginal '6?' (blue ink) beside the reference to curve (1.3) is an annotation, possibly querying the reference or numbering. It is not a mathematical correction.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript copy of Deligne's published 'Formulaire' (LNM 476). All content is published and correctly credited to Deligne/Tate; it is notable only as evidence that Grothendieck kept this text in his Gauss–Manin/Cartier file.
transcription_corrections: The marginal '6?' is a handwritten blue-ink annotation in the right margin next to the line 'forme modulaire entière de poids n s'exprime comme polynôme de'. It is not part of the text.
The circumflexes on 'polynôme' are handwritten additions to the typescript.
The '21' at the bottom is the archive page number written upside down, not part of the text.
